## GPT-5 Prompt Anatomy — OpenAI's six-part role-to-stop-condition template
- Creator: @theaifield | Type: technique | Tier: B | Collection: ai1
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DNTuDtvtZkS/
- Tools: ChatGPT, GPT-5, OpenAI | Techniques: chain-of-thought, context loading, prompt engineering, role prompting, stop conditions, structured output | Domains: LLM, prompt engineering
- A worked example of OpenAI's GPT-5 prompting structure: Role, Task, Context, Reasoning, Output format and Stop conditions, shown on a 'find three under-the-radar hikes near San Francisco' prompt. The useful bits are the explicit self-vetting step and a stop condition that defines when the answer is done.

## Claude Code Team Tips — Boris Cherny's 10 habits for parallel, plan-first agent work

- Karpathy's autoresearch runs continuous keep-or-revert experiments against a measurable target (83 runs, 15 kept); OpenSpace auto-fixes, improves and learns skills from real usage; CLI-Anything wraps apps like GIMP, Blender and Inkscape as CLIs; claude-peers lets separate Claude Code sessions talk; gws is a Google Workspace CLI.

## Ising Model — modeling herd behavior and market phase transitions
- Creator: @quant.dhawan | Type: technique | Tier: B | Collection: quant
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DTsn_IKE06E/
- Tools: Python | Techniques: AI agents, Agent-Based Modeling, Phase Transitions, Symmetry Breaking | Domains: 3D, agents, finance/trading, physics, quant
- 3D lattice visualization of the Ising model applied to financial markets. Blue=sellers, orange=buyers. At high volatility the market is random; as social pressure increases, clusters form leading to spontaneous symmetry breaking (crashes/trends). Built in Python for agent-based modeling.

## Heston Model — stochastic volatility for realistic options pricing
- Creator: @quant.dhawan | Type: technique | Tier: B | Collection: quant
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DW6uAQdk1r0/
- Tools: Python | Techniques: Mean Reversion, Stochastic Volatility, Volatility Smile, algorithmic trading, stochastic modeling | Domains: 3D, derivatives, finance/trading, options, quant
- Explains why Black-Scholes fails (constant vol assumption) and how the Heston Model introduces stochastic volatility. Captures the volatility smile and skew that basic models miss. Essential for options pricing.

## Cox Process — doubly stochastic Poisson for bursty market events
- Creator: @quant.dhawan | Type: technique | Tier: B | Collection: quant
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DW4GU9HE8nd/
- Techniques: Doubly Stochastic Poisson, Intensity Modeling, Point Processes, algorithmic trading, limit orders, stochastic modeling | Domains: finance/trading, quant, stochastic-processes
- Standard Poisson processes assume constant event rates, but markets are bursty. The Cox Process (Doubly Stochastic Poisson) uses a CIR-driven random intensity to model trade arrivals, defaults, and volatility spikes more realistically.

- Simulates the OU process showing mean reversion dynamics with theta (reversion speed), mu (equilibrium), and sigma (noise). Core model for pairs trading, interest rate spreads, and volatility signals in quantitative finance.

## Kalman Filter — adaptive signal extraction for non-stationary markets
- Creator: @quant.dhawan | Type: technique | Tier: A | Collection: quant
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DTfqcYUE2uV/
- Tools: Python | Techniques: Adaptive Filtering, Kalman filter, Non-Stationary Signal Processing, State Estimation, algorithmic trading | Domains: finance/trading, quant, signal processing, video production
- Financial data is non-linear and non-stationary, breaking standard filters. Kalman Filter adapts in real-time, unlike lagging moving averages or FFT (which assumes stationarity). Optimal for real-time signal extraction.

- Applies CWT to QQQ to analyze frequency-domain dynamics over time. Unlike FFT (fixed window), wavelets capture how dominant frequencies shift across regimes. Reveals the market's changing 'heartbeat'.

## Random Matrix Theory — cleaning correlation matrices from noise
- Creator: @quant.dhawan | Type: technique | Tier: A | Collection: quant
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DTXv8W_k-0x/
- Techniques: Eigenvalue Filtering, Marcenko-Pastur Distribution, Random Matrix Theory, algorithmic trading | Domains: finance/trading, linear-algebra, quant, risk
- Standard correlation matrices treat random noise as valid connections. Random Matrix Theory (RMT) filters eigenvalues to 'clean' the matrix, keeping only statistically significant correlations. The market is 90% noise.

## Stable Distribution — modeling fat-tailed crashes beyond Gaussian
- Creator: @quant.dhawan | Type: technique | Tier: B | Collection: quant
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DTSn31Ek2DB/
- Techniques: Extreme Value Theory, Fat Tail Modeling, Monte Carlo, Non-Gaussian Returns, algorithmic trading | Domains: 3D, finance/trading, quant, risk, statistics
- Markets go up slowly but crash fast. Standard Gaussian models underestimate crash probability. Uses Stable (Levy) distributions to properly model fat tail events and Black Swan risks that beginners ignore.

## Hurst Exponent — 3D surface of BTC memory and mean-reversion zones
- Creator: @quant.dhawan | Type: technique | Tier: S | Collection: quant
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DTPrgWIk4Ns/
- Techniques: Fractal Analysis, Hurst exponent, Long-Range Dependence, Rescaled Range Analysis, algorithmic trading | Domains: 3D, crypto, finance/trading, quant, statistics
- Plots the Hurst Exponent of BTC-USD as a 3D surface. H>0.5 = trending (momentum), H<0.5 = mean-reverting, H=0.5 = random walk. Shows how market 'memory' varies across timeframes. Basis for adaptive strategy selection.

## VectorBT Grid Search — mmap data, joblib batching and vectorized backtests
- Creator: @quant.dhawan | Type: technique | Tier: A | Collection: quant
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DTAjTaBADAx/
- Tools: NumPy, Numba, Python, VectorBT, joblib, pandas | Techniques: Vectorized Backtesting, algorithmic trading, backtesting, memory mapping, parallel batching, parameter grid search, vectorized backtesting | Domains: backtesting, data science, finance/trading, python, quant
- A speed recipe for strategy grid searches with VectorBT: load OHLCV via numpy memmap (mmap_mode='r', copy=False) to avoid RAM blowups, fan thousands of backtests across cores with joblib Parallel, batch tasks in groups of 1,000, and run Portfolio.from_signals with fees and slippage as Numba-compiled matrix ops. Illustrated with a BTC moving-average crossover return surface.

## Salvador Dalí on hypnagogic images — 1971 Dick Cavett interview
- Creator: @artrkl_mag | Type: art | Tier: A | Collection: art-i-like
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/CyRQl12u3lv/
- Techniques: hypnagogic image capture | Domains: art, education | Medium: unknown
- Dalí explains to Dick Cavett that his paintings aren't dreams but hypnagogic images — vivid images in the 10–15 minutes before sleep that he 'catches' and paints photographically, with no message or explanation.

## Kintsugi sake-bottle repair — urushi lacquer joins, gold powder finish
- Creator: @saca_kintsugi | Type: technique | Tier: S | Collection: art-i-like
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/Cwmjyr_v_Ne/
- Tools: keshifun gold powder, urushi lacquer | Techniques: hon-kintsugi, mugi-urushi bonding | Domains: art, design | Medium: unknown
- A traditional hon-kintsugi repair of a broken tokkuri (sake flask): crack-stopping and interior repairs are finished first because the narrow neck blocks later access, then shards are glued with mugi-urushi, squeeze-out is trimmed with a design knife, and seams are finished in keshifun gold powder.

## James Stevens Curl on ornament — why art looks bolted onto modernist buildings
- Creator: @caveofapelles | Type: inspiration | Tier: A | Collection: art-i-like
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/CwaBZ2eMK2O/
- Domains: architecture, art, design | Medium: unknown
- Architectural historian James Stevens Curl argues sculpture and decoration were integral to architecture from Greece through Gothic, Renaissance, Rundbogenstil and Egyptian Revival, until modernism removed ornament entirely — so art now feels bolted on as an afterthought.

## Al Bahar Towers — sun-tracking origami façade that halves cooling load
- Creator: @archademy.ai | Type: design | Tier: A | Collection: art-i-like
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/CwNnre_Ih9l/
- Techniques: biomimicry, kinetic façade, parametric shading | Domains: architecture, art, design | Medium: unknown
- Aedas Architects' 2008 Abu Dhabi towers wrap the glass in computer-controlled umbrella-like screens modeled on the mashrabiya lattice and on biomimicry (pupils, flowers). The panels unfold with the sun, cutting glare and glass heat and reportedly halving air-conditioning demand.

## Frei Otto — lightweight tensile structures found from soap bubbles
- Creator: @parametric.architecture | Type: resource | Tier: A | Collection: art-i-like
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/CwNkyKyIVMW/
- Techniques: form finding, physical modeling, tensile membrane structures | Domains: architecture, art, design | Medium: unknown
- Profile of German architect-engineer Frei Otto (1925-2015), Pritzker 2015 winner and founder of Stuttgart's Institute for Lightweight Structures. He form-found membrane and cable-net roofs from soap films, bird skulls and spider webs; works include the 1972 Munich Olympic Stadium and the 1967 Montreal Expo pavilion.

## Decalcomania — surrealist paint-transfer for chance-driven portraits
- Creator: @scumchoir | Type: technique | Tier: A | Collection: art-i-like
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/Cnfmkm-q4dC/
- Techniques: controlled chance, decalcomania | Domains: art, design | Medium: unknown
- The artist explains decalcomania, Oscar Domínguez's surrealist method of pressing paint between surfaces to transfer random textures. They start with a rough portrait silhouette, let the transfer create the texture, then commit to it and pull form and dimension out of the splotches.

## Kronos — open foundation model that tokenizes candlesticks to forecast markets
- Creator: @gigaqian | Type: repo | Tier: S | Collection: stock2
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DW2hy6EDqt-/
- Tools: Kronos | Techniques: K-line tokenization, algorithmic trading, autoregressive forecasting, time series foundation model | Domains: LLM, crypto, finance/trading, quant, video production
- Walkthrough of Kronos, a free time-series foundation model from a Tsinghua PhD student that forecasts stocks and crypto. It tokenizes K-lines (OHLC plus volume) into discrete tokens and trains an autoregressive model on them, so it generalizes like an LLM over market data.

## Concise outputs beat verbosity — study behind the caveman prompting trend
- Creator: @chase.h.ai | Type: technique | Tier: A | Collection: ai6
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DW19mg8x78m/
- Tools: Claude, Claude Code | Techniques: AI agents, brevity constraints, caveman prompting, code generation | Domains: LLM, agents, open source, prompt engineering, software development
- A study of 31 open-weight models on 1,500 problems found small models beat much larger ones on ~8% of problems, but forcing the big models to be concise reversed it. Ties into the caveman repo that makes Claude Code talk tersely; the claim is brevity improves accuracy, not just token cost, possibly undoing RLHF-learned over-explaining.

- Creator: @anna.zhang | Type: art | Tier: B | Collection: ai7
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DYQi0JAqScX/
- Techniques: arbitrage, frame differencing, mean reversion, stochastic modeling, temporal motion filtering | Domains: architecture, art, creative coding, finance/trading, photography, software development, video production

## Surface Tension — optical tweezers and ComfyUI depth layers on living cells
- Creator: @zerospacelabs | Type: art | Tier: A | Collection: ai7

## Cyberdeck privacy stack — GrapheneOS, Tails, Orange Pi and rotating-IMSI carrier
- Creator: @lizthedeveloper | Type: resource | Tier: A | Collection: ai7
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DYShNwIDzTK/

- This is an opinionated privacy kit for going 'digitally off-grid'. It includes a self-built cyberdeck on a Rockchip-based Orange Pi, a Linux distro that doesn't ask for age verification, and GrapheneOS with the camera and accelerometer disabled. ## Claude -p and Agent SDK billing split — what the June 15 change means

## Self-improving startup — Loom transcripts to Claude skills to scheduled tasks
- Creator: @angus.sewell | Type: technique | Tier: A | Collection: ai7
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DYxDK5ixq07/
- Tools: Claude, Hermes Agent, Loom, Obsidian | Techniques: scheduled agents, self-healing skills, skill authoring from transcripts | Domains: agents, productivity, prompt engineering, video production
- A recipe for automating a repetitive business. First run each process by hand and record it on Loom. Then feed each transcript to Claude to write a skill, run the skills manually and patch them when they fail, and finally put each skill on a scheduled task. As an advanced step, skills log their own failures and a meta-skill fixes the others, in the spirit of YC's 'self-improving startup' and Hermes Agent.

## NVIDIA RTX Spark — ARM SoC with unified memory for local agents
- Creator: @gigaqian | Type: news | Tier: B | Collection: ai7
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DZD_aFIptpw/
- Tools: NVIDIA RTX Spark, Windows | Techniques: system on a chip, unified memory | Domains: design, hardware, news, video production
- At GTC Taipei, NVIDIA unveiled RTX Spark, an ARM-based system-on-chip for Windows. It combines a 20-core CPU, a Blackwell GPU and up to 128 GB of unified memory on one chip, so large models can run locally, and more than 30 laptops and 10 desktops have been announced. Trade-offs include slower memory than discrete setups and Prism emulation for x86 apps.

## Graphify — turn a repo into a knowledge graph to cut Claude Code tokens

## Project-management loop for agents — tasks, context checks, skill mining

## Equations as images — color vectors that store parametric art in TouchDesigner
- Creator: @as.ws__ | Type: technique | Tier: A | Collection: creative
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DSqaoDMEpaJ/
- Tools: TouchDesigner | Techniques: color as vector, data textures, parametric equations | Domains: art, creative coding
- Because color is a vector, an image can encode an equation, so y=x² becomes a black-to-yellow gradient. Rows or columns of an image can hold whole sets of parametric equations. The artist uses textures as equation stores in TouchDesigner to build forms like jellyfish, and explains it in a DATLAB NYC talk.

## CoreWeave debt explained — how GPU-backed loans fund the neoclouds
- Creator: @thewallstreetskinny | Type: resource | Tier: A | Collection: ai8
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DehLFj6ON6C/
- Tools: Anthropic, OpenAI | Techniques: asset-backed financing, project finance | Domains: crypto, design, finance/trading, news, video production
- An ex-Morgan Stanley CDO structurer explains the neocloud stack (landlords, vertically integrated players like IREN and Crusoe, CoreWeave, Nebius) and why CoreWeave's GPU-backed asset financing spooked markets. Advance rates hit 90-95% against off-taker credit, and loan, contract and GPU useful life are nearly the same length, leaving a thin tail.

## ln + vpype — 3D scenes to hidden-line vector art for pen plotters
- Creator: @index.opensource | Type: repo | Tier: S | Collection: ai8
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/Dd9Uvy9ByCE/
- Tools: ln, vpype | Techniques: CSG, hidden-line removal, path optimization, ray casting | Domains: 3D, animation, art, creative coding, open source
- Michael Fogleman's ln (Go) renders 3D scenes as 2D vector paths by ray-testing each path segment for visibility, supporting CSG, math surfaces and procedural cities. vpype then merges and sorts paths for plotting, cutting pen-up travel 86% in this example. Both MIT licensed, output straight to SVG.

## Quake III fast inverse square root — the 0x5f3759df bit hack explained
- Creator: @mygearhut | Type: resource | Tier: A | Collection: ai8
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DeHSjhOAMwe/
- Tools: Quake III Arena | Techniques: Newton-Raphson iteration, code generation, float bit reinterpretation | Domains: 3D, education, software development
- Explains Quake III's four-line fast inverse square root: reinterpret float bits as an integer (which behaves logarithmically), shift right to halve the exponent, subtract from magic constant 0x5f3759df, then one Newton-Raphson step to bring error under 0.175%. Covers why normalization was costly on 1999 Pentiums and the constant's lineage through 3dfx and Cleve Moler.

## Conway's law — Casey Muratori on the one unbreakable rule, now for agents
- Creator: @ryanlpeterman | Type: resource | Tier: A | Collection: creative4
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DdY7NUbDys2/
- Techniques: work partitioning | Domains: agents, architecture, design, gaming, software development, video production
- Casey Muratori argues Conway's law is software's only real law: once you split work among workers (people or agents) whose communication is slower than their internal compute, design iteration across that boundary is locked in as slower. 'Products look like the org chart' is a consequence, not the law itself.

## GENIUS Act stablecoins — how banks keep the T-bill yield on your cash
- Creator: @alexanderelorenzo | Type: resource | Tier: B | Collection: stock3

- Tools: Binance, USYC | Techniques: algorithmic trading, repurchase agreements, tokenized treasuries | Domains: crypto, finance/trading
- Under the GENIUS Act banks can issue stablecoins, park the backing cash in short-term Treasury bills, keep the roughly 4% yield (the law bars passing it to holders), and repo the T-bills for liquidity. ## Workflow hijacking — Noma research on AI automations with no authorization

## Booking.com AI observability — Kafka buffer and PII redaction before Arize
- Creator: @therobertta | Type: resource | Tier: A | Collection: ai8
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/Dcl3dEJAjo0/
- Tools: Arize, Kafka | Techniques: LLM tracing, PII redaction, fine-tuning, message-bus decoupling | Domains: architecture, data science, security, software development
- Walkthrough of Booking.com's GenAI telemetry architecture: apps emit traces to a collector, which normalizes them onto a managed Kafka bus (durable buffer decoupling producers and consumers), through a dedicated PII-redaction service that masks span attributes and text, then out to Arize for real-time monitoring and a warehouse for offline analytics and backfills. A second pipeline ships ML prediction logs to Arize for ranking and fraud models.

## Backpropagation visualized — gradients as downhill steps on the loss surface
- Creator: @techvrix | Type: resource | Tier: B | Collection: ai8
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DcXQeNGkY6a/
- Techniques: backpropagation, chain rule, gradient descent | Domains: data science, education
- Welch Labs explainer clip: estimate how loss changes per parameter (e.g. nudging m2 from 0 to 0.1 drops loss from 2.45 to 2.24), combine all partial derivatives into the gradient, and step against it; backprop uses the chain rule to compute that gradient efficiently across the network.

## Prime Agent — self-rewriting harness lifts Opus 5 to 95.5% on ARC-AGI-3
- Creator: @wassimyounes_ | Type: repo | Tier: A | Collection: creative

## Kronos — transformer that reads candlesticks as a language (part 3)
- Creator: @gigaqian | Type: resource | Tier: A | Collection: creative
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DW7thNGDrPJ/
- Tools: Kronos | Techniques: autoregressive decoding, binary spherical quantization, self-attention | Domains: LLM, creative coding, finance/trading, quant, video production
- Final part of a Kronos explainer: after binary spherical quantization and hierarchical encoding turn candles into tokens, a transformer uses self-attention (query/key/value per candle) to weight relevant bars like a volume spike over chop, and an autoregressive decoder predicts the next tokens, i.e. future price action. Contrasts with sequential LSTMs.

## Conway's Law — your product ships your org chart

- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DbSjJT7sLUf/
- Techniques: reverse Conway maneuver | Domains: architecture, design, music, software development, video production
- Melvin Conway's 1967 observation: systems copy the communication structure of the organization that builds them. Modern teams apply the reverse Conway maneuver, designing the target architecture first and then shaping teams to match.

## Shell sort — gap-based insertion sort that moves items far early
- Creator: @algo.andre | Type: technique | Tier: B | Collection: ai8
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DaSql3FhvG5/
- Techniques: insertion sort, shell sort | Domains: education, software development
- Shell sort runs insertion sort on elements separated by a shrinking gap, letting small values travel long distances early. By the final gap-1 pass the list is nearly sorted, so insertion sort finishes quickly.

## Quantum reservoir computing — nine atoms forecasting weather
- Creator: @gigaqian | Type: news | Tier: B | Collection: ai8
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DWxNZMrjqY9/
- Techniques: fading memory, reservoir computing | Domains: data science, news, video production
- USTC researchers in Hefei built a quantum reservoir computer from nine interacting atoms that beat classical baselines on weather prediction. The reservoir needs no training, only the readout is trained, and quantum noise is used as the fading memory that time-series forecasting needs.

## Cochlea — Wi-Fi side-channel attack on Ring cameras

## Time complexity patterns — ten loop shapes to recognize in interviews
- Creator: @algomasterio | Type: resource | Tier: B | Collection: ai8
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/Dau64tdyY4n/
- Techniques: code generation, complexity analysis | Domains: education, software development
- Cheat sheet mapping code shapes to Big-O: hash lookup O(1), halving loop O(log n), single and sequential loops O(n) and O(n+m), loop plus binary search and divide-and-conquer O(n log n), nested and triangular loops O(n²), branching recursion exponential, permutations O(n!).

## Hoffman's interface theory — perception as a desktop, not reality

## Glenn Gould's humming — thinking music away from the piano
- Creator: @dailyhistoryclips | Type: art | Tier: B | Collection: creative4
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DdYbBL5IlNq/
- Techniques: mental practice | Domains: audio, music
- Glenn Gould hummed audibly on nearly every recording despite Columbia engineers' mic tricks. He traced it to practising under a vacuum cleaner's noise, which taught him to hear pieces internally and learn away from the instrument; the voice is the overflow, audible on the Goldberg Variations.

## Hand-cut kitchen tile mosaic — materials and process from a first build

- The Elizabeth Greenshields Foundation gives CAD 17,000 first grants (20,000 on renewal) to early-career representational artists worldwide, with no fee, no CV and rolling applications by post. The Awesome Foundation's $1,000 monthly micro-grants (US, UK, Australia, Canada chapters) are the fallback for abstract or non-painting work.

## Turing patterns — why reaction-diffusion gives us five fingers
- Creator: @ri_science | Type: resource | Tier: B | Collection: creative4
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DbKwrrkjd7U/
- Techniques: reaction-diffusion | Domains: creative coding, education
- Philip Ball (Royal Institution talk) explains that digit count is set during embryonic development by Alan Turing's 1952 reaction-diffusion mechanism: interacting chemical signals self-organize into regular stripes that become fingers. ## DeepPIV laser-sheet scanning — 3D models of deep-sea siphonophores in situ
- Creator: @howtown_videos | Type: technique | Tier: A | Collection: creative4
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/Da20EPjsSNP/
- Tools: DeepPIV | Techniques: laser sheet imaging, volumetric reconstruction | Domains: 3D, education, hardware, video production
- Schmidt Ocean Institute's ROV on the Falkor (too) uses MBARI's DeepPIV system: a laser flattened into a thin sheet is swept through semi-transparent animals to capture planes that stack into full 3D reconstructions, without killing the specimen. The subject is a siphonophore, a colony of specialized zooids acting as one animal.

## HFT short-term reversal — buy weekly losers, sell winners across 4,500 stocks
- Creator: @7am.research | Type: technique | Tier: B | Collection: quant
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DWu_CQnjZjn/
- Techniques: algorithmic trading, arbitrage, high-frequency trading, short-term reversal, statistical arbitrage | Domains: finance/trading, quant
- A 60 Minutes clip with Manoj Narang describing a cross-sectional mean-reversion test: buy $5 of stocks down 5% last week, sell $10 of stocks up 10%, across the whole ~4,500-stock universe at once. Near 50% win rate per trade but no losing month thanks to breadth and speed, with Joe Saluzzi arguing it rigs the game.

## Efficiency-ratio forecaster — skip choppy days to lift a strategy's metrics
- Creator: @telonicstrading | Type: technique | Tier: A | Collection: stock2
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DeF5_5yPtDb/
- Techniques: Kaufman efficiency ratio, algorithmic trading, logistic regression, regime gating | Domains: data science, finance/trading, quant
- Instead of predicting direction, a logistic regression on 15 price features forecasts the next day's Kaufman efficiency ratio (trendiness versus chop). Trades on predicted low-efficiency days made about a third of the money, so gating them out improved nearly every metric and held on two years of out-of-sample data.

## Overnight vs intraday returns — Knuteson's 'Strikingly Suspicious' anomaly
- Creator: @quantpapers | Type: resource | Tier: S | Collection: stock2
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DeF6WMaB-NX/
- Techniques: algorithmic trading, overnight drift, return decomposition | Domains: finance/trading, quant
- Bruce Knuteson (ex-MIT physicist, D. E. Shaw) splits each day into close-to-open and open-to-close: Micron since 1990 is +138M% overnight and -99.9% intraday, and the same sawtooth shows in 21 indices (China reversed). His paper 'Strikingly Suspicious Overnight and Intraday Returns' rejects earnings and news as explanations and alleges large firms push prices at the open; it's a claim, not a proof.

The Munger attribution and the personal P&L claims are unverified, and the link is gated behind a comment.

## 2010 Flash Crash — how Navinder Sarao spoofed E-mini S&P futures
- Creator: @thestockguytwitch | Type: news | Tier: B | Collection: stock2
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DYnlB8vJC56/

## Charlie Munger's inversion — solve problems by asking how to cause failure
- Creator: @charliemungerhub | Type: technique | Tier: A | Collection: stock3
- URL: https://www.instagram.com/p/DbYp-bgTBBA/
- Techniques: inversion, mental models | Domains: finance/trading, productivity
- Munger explains inversion with his WWII meteorologist job: ask how you'd kill pilots (icing, running out of fuel), then avoid those. Same move for any problem: list what would hurt it most and steer clear.

## Red-Team Your Own Agent — prompt-injection CI from the jailbreak corpus
- Class: emergent_capability
- Quality: 5/5
- Difficulty: Medium
- Thesis: The catalog holds both halves of a loop nobody has closed. On one side sit offense corpora and autonomous attackers — L1B3RT4S still landing on GPT-5, an agent that goes from one sentence to a verified exploit, scanners hunting exposed AI servers. On the other sit the pipes that pour untrusted text into your agent — Agent Reach reading Reddit and X, 90k-skill hubs, one-command skill installers. Point the attacker inward and you get prompt-injection CI — every skill install and harness change gets replayed against a jailbreak-and-hijack suite before it touches your keys.
- Entries: DOPqBfyDMHG, DdKKSaANJm7, DaGEbyAAHOo, Dd6izTYiln1, Db0vxQexdJI, DXcWjL0jLsd, DYX_M8yx6r4, DX4qpEHxY7g
- Action: Build a 50-case suite this week — 20 L1B3RT4S-style jailbreaks, 20 Noma-style 'just ask for the data' hijacks planted in fake Reddit/X posts fetched via Agent Reach, 10 sponsored-option nudges — and run it against your harness with a canary secret in the environment
Wire it as a pre-install hook: any new skill from find-skills or a skills hub gets diffed, then the suite reruns with that skill loaded; fail the install if the canary leaks or a tool call goes outside the allowlist
Add the sandboxing layer from the portfolio-projects post — per-skill capability manifests (network, filesystem, secrets) — and measure how many suite cases each manifest blocks
Falsifier: if a plain allowlist on outbound tool calls blocks ≥95% of the suite with no skill-level testing, the CI layer is overkill and a static policy file is the whole answer

## Skills That Earn Their Lines — benchmark-gated self-editing plus subtraction
- Class: workflow_multiplier
- Quality: 5/5
- Difficulty: Medium
- Thesis: Successor to the harness and second-brain dives. Those stop at 'append a lesson after every mistake'. The catalog now holds the missing machinery — Microsoft SkillOpt rewrites skills only when a benchmark improves, bilevel autoresearch adds a coach loop over the worker, Prime Agent rewrites its own harness to 95.5% on ARC-AGI-3 — and, crucially, evidence that subtraction matters as much as addition: Boris Cherny's simple mode and the setup-purge post show stale rules make newer models dumber. Combine them into a ratchet that both adds and deletes rules, keeping only edits that beat a held-out eval.
- Entries: DbEK3bustQ7, DbjLy_tormR, DbtJytsumrO, Dcgr7YiIXD9, DZnY2vaxWRF, Dd1cWobxn7n, DcMSk7Rxcdu, Dbhuaw7Pk4u
- Action: Export your last 3 months of Claude history, have a small model tag 40 representative tasks with pass/fail criteria — that is your held-out eval
Run an ablation sweep: drop each CLAUDE.md rule and skill one at a time, rerun the eval, delete anything whose removal does not hurt the score
Add the SkillOpt loop on a nightly cron — skills log issues, an optimizer proposes edits, only score-improving edits merge; export passing traces for a Soup fine-tune later
Falsifier: if eval scores vary more between two identical runs than between best and worst rule sets, your eval is too noisy and the whole ratchet is optimizing noise

## Anything With Geometry — Ink on Paper: the Pen-Plotter Loop
- Class: creative_fusion
- Quality: 5/5
- Difficulty: Medium
- Thesis: Fogleman's ln turns any 3D scene into hidden-line vector paths, and vpype makes those paths plotter-ready. Everything else in the catalog that produces geometry — a phone scan, a ripped PS1 level, a ray-marched fractal, a strange attractor, the phase-space shape of BTC volatility, a Blender scene an agent wrote in Python — becomes a source for that one pipe. The output is a physical ink original, and in a market drowning in free pixels that is the scarce thing.
- Entries: Dd9Uvy9ByCE, DeuZ4BnhCqA, DbqLB-zMoJR, DbcEatOsXG2, DbU9ysVITFS, DehlIB2PT4h, DYsSz2rvWGI, DTLkCVXE7O6
- Action: Week 1: install ln (Go) and vpype; have Claude Code write a script that loads an OBJ (start with a DuckStation PS1 rip or a phone scan) into ln, sets camera and texture paths, and exports SVG; run vpype linemerge/linesort and preview
Week 2: add two math sources — a Thomas attractor and a 3-lag phase-space embedding of a year of BTC daily volatility — emitted as 3D polylines straight into ln; make a 6-print series titled by date range
Week 3: plot the series on an A3 pen plotter (AxiDraw-class or a DIY drawing machine) with two pen weights, photograph per the print-on-demand guide, list originals plus POD reproductions, and submit to one grant
Falsifier: if scanned or ripped meshes produce unreadable line mush unless you hand-pick every path, or if plotted originals cannot sell above the POD print price, the loop is a toy, not a practice

## Strategy Autoresearch — the judge is the product, not the agent
- Class: workflow_multiplier
- Quality: 5/5
- Difficulty: Medium
- Thesis: Self-rewriting loops (Karpathy-style autoresearch, bilevel coach loops, Microsoft SkillOpt) keep any edit that beats a benchmark. Point one at trading and it becomes an industrial overfitting machine — the backtest is the benchmark, and the loop will beat it ten thousand times. The quant saves already hold the fix: probability of backtest overfitting, permutation tests, transaction costs and backtest-to-live drift. Wire those in as the loop's judge, and use the loop's own log as the exact count of trials — the number human quants never know.
- Entries: DbEK3bustQ7, DbjLy_tormR, DeNnxp5v_Fu, DTZyMVPiHM5, DT8BX8vEzHm, DWjr0x3Deom, DUx9t_FE0CY, DeW79CbCkO3
- Action: Wrap a vectorized backtester (VectorBT) in a SkillOpt-style loop where Claude proposes strategy edits and every proposal is appended to a trials table with its parameters and result.
Replace 'beats benchmark' with a judge that needs all four: positive after realistic fees, beats 95% of a permutation null, deflated Sharpe positive using the trials-table count, and a held-out year scored once at the end.
Have a second model (Codex or GPT) audit each surviving strategy's code for look-ahead bias before it reaches paper trading; monitor live drift with Wasserstein distance and auto-retire on breach.
falsifier: seed the loop with pure-noise synthetic prices. If anything passes the judge, the judge is broken — fix it before you show it a real market.

## Ambient Executive Function — glanceable hardware for agents and attention
- Class: life_leverage
- Quality: 5/5
- Difficulty: Easy
- Thesis: OpenAI built a $230 hardware controller for babysitting coding agents. Someone answered with a MacBook-notch status app, and Bot Crossing turned 80 agents into characters who raise their hands. Separately, NFC stickers make logging a habit a one-tap physical act, and Sharp memory LCDs stay on for days at e-paper power. Combine them into a small always-on desk object that shows what needs you, both agents waiting for approval and your own NOW list, and takes physical taps as input. That turns 'out of sight, out of mind' from a willpower problem into an environment.
- Entries: DbIxSSaEtGd, DbaFoAUMvnK, DczR-QlSMdK, DcJNZeBxR2D, DZoREIHtMjL, DctoIMltaNN, DWBEMihjWp7, DdKLjDHlG0c
- Action: Build an ESP32 + 2.7in Sharp memory LCD in a printed stand; it polls a tiny endpoint serving (a) top 3 lines of NOW.md, (b) count of agent sessions awaiting approval via a Claude Code Notification/Stop hook.
Stick NFC tags on desk, water bottle and door: tap = 'done/started/leaving', logged by an iOS Shortcut to the same endpoint; the display updates within seconds.
Run 14 days logging glance-triggered actions (taps within 2 min of a display change) and agent wait time before/after.
Falsifier: if glance-triggered actions fall to near zero by week two (habituation) and agent wait time doesn't drop, ambient display isn't beating a phone notification.

## Earned Autonomy — a three-tier router that demotes work to your own GPU
- Class: arbitrage_opportunity
- Quality: 4/5
- Difficulty: Medium
- Thesis: Three trends in the catalog point at one design. Orchestrator-worker splits (Fable plans, Opus or GPT-5.6 executes) cut frontier spend. A 27B Qwen now fits a single 24GB card and posts agentic benchmarks that were frontier-only a year ago, while open-token share flipped to 80/20 in twelve weeks. And vendors can change the deal overnight — Anthropic killed subscription tokens in third-party tools. The agentic OS blueprint's 'earned autonomy' is the missing link: let each task class graduate down the stack — frontier, mid-tier, local — as its review pass rate proves it can.
- Entries: Da1hOm7scjR, DamEcWuPvX0, DaojVuSNKno, DeW79CbCkO3, DcCdYgnJ10h, DbjmqTYJfMY, DeIOphnT7Yq, DVKJlJYEsmm
- Action: Log every delegated task for two weeks with a class label (rename, test-writing, data cleanup, UI tweak) and the reviewer's pass/fail
Stand up Qwen 27B via llama.cpp or Ollama behind the same subagent interface; route one low-stakes class to it in shadow mode and grade it with the same frontier reviewer
Add the promotion rule: 20 consecutive passes moves a class one tier down, any fail moves it back up; track dollars saved per class
Falsifier: if after a month no task class sustains a 90%+ pass rate on the local tier, the local floor is not there yet for your work — stay two-tier

## Capture the Room Twice — Splat Scans and Song for Roots Music
- Class: creative_fusion
- Quality: 4/5
- Difficulty: Medium
- Thesis: Roots musicians already treat the room as an instrument — testing a 200-year-old house's resonance, filming tunes on porches and in old venues, the way Lomax filmed singers in their own kitchens. A phone can now capture that room as a Gaussian splat, and Gausseous makes the splat react to audio in a browser. Record the room's acoustics in the same session and the sound and the image come from one capture of one place.
- Entries: DUOwelij-pU, DOwuQwPkeVm, DajBiyRpCr6, 891906d4212e, DbU9ysVITFS, DcicSv_J7vo, Da20EPjsSNP, CvsDXJbJh6O

Cut a 60-second vertical piece — real performance footage intercut with the reacting splat — and A/B it against a plain performance video on the same account
Falsifier: if low-light interior scans come out too noisy to read, or the splat cut loses watch-through to the plain performance video, the format is a gimmick

## Melody Genealogy — Crate-Digging the Public Domain with Local Search

Point that pattern at Lomax, Prelinger and 78-rpm archives with audio embeddings, and you get a tune family tree plus cleared public-domain samples, each with provenance.

## Own the Thermometer — $100 sensors as prediction-market edge
- Class: arbitrage_opportunity
- Quality: 4/5
- Difficulty: Medium
- Thesis: A student cleared $100K+ on Polymarket weather contracts with a dorm-built weather station, and a separate trader harvests contracts already sitting at 99c. Cheap sensors plus an agent that watches the order book in the final hours turn that into a repeatable process. A student cleared $100K+ on Polymarket weather contracts with a dorm-built weather station.
- Entries: DWzz7T9Ddex, DWEfIS9jRgI, DWrQKaskWlZ, Dd6W2q5gZJ-, DW6Ny_zkqSY, DccLLkoPCT1, DUrQ187EvI4, Dd4Ca8oiiyB

falsifier: if the official station's public intra-hour feed already moves the price as fast as your sensor does, your sensor adds nothing — the edge was always the dorm student's local microclimate, not a method.

## Forecast the Weather, Not the Price — gating models by tradeability
- Class: emergent_capability
- Quality: 4/5
- Difficulty: Medium
- Thesis: Open candlestick foundation models like Kronos give you a forecast on every bar, and a hedge-fund stress test says it fails on many levels. A separate save shows the better question: a small logistic regression that predicts tomorrow's efficiency ratio (trend versus chop) and skips the choppy days lifted almost every metric over two years out of sample. Physics-flavored measures in the quant collection — Lempel-Ziv compressibility, Hurst exponent, Lyapunov exponent, hidden Markov regimes — are all measures of the same thing: is this market forecastable right now? Use them as a confidence gate on the foundation model, not as signals.
- Entries: DeF5_5yPtDb, DWz7VPXjr5V, DW7thNGDrPJ, DW-TOhIDgjh, DUTQPorEwuP, DTPrgWIk4Ns, DTiLFogE4KT, DW1kTMcExSj
- Action: Run Kronos zero-shot on two years of hourly BTC and QQQ and log every forecast with its realized error.
Compute rolling efficiency ratio, Lempel-Ziv complexity and Hurst for each bar, bucket bars into tradeability quintiles, and plot Kronos error per quintile.
If error falls across quintiles, fit the efficiency-ratio-style logistic model to predict next-period tradeability and paper-trade Kronos only in the top bucket.
falsifier: if Kronos error is flat across tradeability quintiles, the complexity measures say nothing about this model's skill and the gate is decoration.

## Scan, Fit, Print — agents that design parts around real objects
- Class: emergent_capability
- Quality: 4/5

## Mission Control for 80 Agents — Conway's law meets game UI
- Class: creative_fusion

## The AI Capex Stack — reading it like a credit analyst
- Class: emergent_capability
- Quality: 3/5

- Thesis: An ex-Morgan Stanley structurer explains that CoreWeave-style GPU loans have a thin tail: loan, contract and GPU useful life are nearly the same length, so the bull case rests on hourly rental prices after contracts end. ## Mocap as Reward — teaching cheap robots to move like you
- Class: emergent_capability
- Quality: 3/5
- Difficulty: Experimental
- Thesis: The Microduck RL demo shows the classic failure: a loose reward function makes the robot 'stand' in a way nobody intended. The catalog also holds the fix, scattered across collections. FreeMoCap turns a webcam into markerless motion capture, HY-Motion produces motion from text on robot skeletons, and Blender plus a GPU contact solver can rehearse physical contact. Use captured or generated motion as an imitation reward on a cheap open robot. The reward-design trial and error becomes 'show it what you mean'.
- Entries: DdCBqmzJgbW, DYAI_fCuvrY, Tencent-Hunyuan/HY-Motion-1.0, DacssZfNGNS, DYuY_-7Oqk4, DXvvNRssb64, C3X9J-wCQps
- Action: Reproduce the Microduck standing run in its sim with 4,096 envs; confirm the reward hack.
Record a 10-second webcam clip of a 'bob and look around' motion with FreeMoCap (or generate one with HY-Motion), retarget to Microduck's joints, and add a pose-tracking imitation term to the reward.
Compare policies: reward-only vs reward + imitation, scored by a blind viewer on 'looks intentional' and by joint-tracking error; deploy the winner to hardware if you have it.
Falsifier: if retargeting human motion to a duck-scale robot body produces infeasible joint targets that the policy can't track better than the plain reward, the motion prior is the wrong shape for small robots.
